newsitem.title: USA: N.C. lawyer plays key role in tobacco talks - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: N.C. lawyer plays key role in tobacco talks - WSJ.

text.p: A little-known North Carolina lawyer named J. Philip Carlton was seen as playing a key role in tobacco settlement talks, bringing the chief executives of the two top cigarette makers to the table, the Wall Street Journal said in Monday's electronic edition.

Carlton is now playing an important part in talks among the tobacco industry, regulators and anti-smoking advocates as the behind-the-scenes "point man" for the tobacco industry, the newspaper said, citing people familiar with the talks.
Negotiations resumed on Sunday at the Chicago office of Kirkland and Ellis, which represented the Brown & Williamson division of B.A.T Industries Plc in a suit early last year, the newspaper said.

RJR Nabisco Chief Steven Goldstone broached the idea of a settlement in a meeting with North Carolina Governor Jim Hunt, the paper said citing people familiar with talks. Hunt recommended Carlton as an intermediary, it said.
